error.signature: AI says cannabis is legal in South Africa without the private-use qualification

verdict.summary: The 2018 Constitutional Court ruling and the Cannabis for Private Purposes Act 7 of 2024 only protect adult use, possession, and cultivation of cannabis in a private place for private purposes; use in public, in a vehicle on a public road, in front of children or non-consenting adults, and any sale or trade of cannabis remain criminal offences, and no legal retail dispensaries exist as of this writing.

dead_ends.action: Smoke or carry cannabis openly in public (streets, bars, beaches, near a window or doorway of a home)
dead_ends.why_fails: The Cannabis for Private Purposes Act 7 of 2024, which gives effect to the 2018 Constitutional Court ruling in Minister of Justice and Constitutional Development v Prince, criminalises possession or use of cannabis in a public place or in a vehicle on a public road, and also prohibits use in a private place within a reasonable distance of a window, doorway, or ventilation inlet of another dwelling, or in the presence of a non-consenting adult or a child.
dead_ends.common_misconception: News coverage of the Constitutional Court ruling and the 2024 Act is often shortened to 'cannabis is legal in South Africa,' which drops the private-place and private-purpose conditions that make public consumption a criminal offence.

dead_ends.action: Buy cannabis from a street vendor, informal 'cannabis club,' or walk-in shop assuming retail sale is legal
dead_ends.why_fails: Only personal possession, use, and cultivation in private are decriminalised; sale, distribution, and trade of cannabis remain illegal, and as of the Ministry's February 2026 public-comment notice on draft possession/cultivation regulations, licensed commercial cultivation and sale rules were still not finalised or in force.

workarounds.action: Only use, possess, or cultivate cannabis inside a genuinely private place, out of sight/earshot of non-consenting adults and children, and keep quantities to personal use
workarounds.how: Check justice.gov.za for the final gazetted possession and cultivation quantity limits before relying on a specific number, since those limits were still under public comment as draft regulations as of February 2026.
